newsitem.title: UK: British manufacturing expands more slowly in December.
newsitem.headline: British manufacturing expands more slowly in December.

text.p: British manufacturing expanded in December for the seventh consecutive month, but at a slower rate than in November as the stronger pound undermined exports, according to a survey published Thursday.
The Purchasing Managers' Survey, conducted by the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply, showed that the sector was continuing to grow steadily and prices were still falling.

The Purchasing Managers' Index, regarded as a reliable barometer of manufacturing activity, dipped to a seasonally adjusted 52.5 percent in December from 54.2 in November. A reading above 50 shows manufacturing is expanding.

"The Purchasing Managers' Index signalled expansion of the manufacturing economy for the seventh month running in December as both output and employment rose to meet further improvements in order books," the CIPS said.

"However, although order levels rose on the whole, driven by an acceleration in the rate of growth of demand for both consumer goods and capital goods, the PMI was weakened by a modest deceleration in the overall rate of growth of order books."

This was due to the stronger pound resulting in weaker growth in export markets for the second month in a row. In addition, December saw an acceleration in the rate at which companies cleared stocks of unsold goods from their shelves.

Michael Jack, financial secretary to the Treasury, said the survey showed Britain was on track to grow more quickly than any other major European economy this year while cost pressures remained under control.
